England.difference_en: England Years 1-2 explicitly use position language and whole, half and quarter turns before later coordinate work.
England.why_en: Verbal descriptions of relative position and turn can establish spatial relationships before coordinate notation is introduced.
England.classroom_use_en: Give movement instructions orally, then ask pupils to draw the same route.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grades 1-6 do not have a standalone position-and-direction strand equivalent to England's early progression; related spatial ideas are distributed across geometry and coordinate work.
US.why_en: This is a curriculum-organisation difference rather than a missing classroom activity.
US.classroom_use_en: Show related geometry standards, but label that there is no directly equivalent standalone Common Core strand.

England.difference_en: England Year 4 uses coordinates in the first quadrant and Year 6 extends to all four quadrants. China's third learning stage uses ordered pairs to locate positions.
England.why_en: Coordinates compress horizontal and vertical positions into an ordered pair, so order matters.
England.classroom_use_en: Use the rule 'across first, then up/down' and ask why swapping coordinates changes the point.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 5 formally represents and interprets points in the first quadrant; Grade 6 extends coordinate work across four quadrants with negative numbers.
US.why_en: Coordinate work develops from two number lines and connects with the rational-number progression.
US.classroom_use_en: Build the coordinate plane from two number lines and identify which coordinate comes from which axis.

England.difference_en: England progressively recognises and completes line-symmetric figures across Years 2-4. China's third learning stage continues axial-symmetry work.
England.why_en: Symmetry is an exact reflection relationship, not simply visual balance.
England.classroom_use_en: Verify a symmetry line by folding or checking that corresponding points are equal distances from it.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 4 explicitly identifies line-symmetric figures and draws lines of symmetry.
US.why_en: Symmetry is developed as a property of figures rather than as part of a full transformation system.
US.classroom_use_en: Include a figure that looks balanced but does not have matching reflected points and ask pupils to test it.

England.difference_en: England Years 5-6 explicitly describes and represents translations while preserving size and orientation. China's third learning stage also develops translation.
England.why_en: A translation moves every point by the same displacement without turning or reflecting the figure.
England.classroom_use_en: Describe a move as '4 right, 2 up' and check that every vertex has the same displacement.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grades 1-6 do not contain a systematic translation-as-transformation strand; formal rigid transformations are developed mainly in Grade 8.
US.why_en: There is no direct Common Core primary standard equivalent to China's primary translation work.
US.classroom_use_en: If translation is used as an extension, label it accurately rather than assigning a fabricated Common Core Grade 5 or 6 match.

England.difference_en: England begins with turn language in the early years and uses rotation more explicitly in upper-primary position and movement work. China's third learning stage also develops rotation.
England.why_en: A precise rotation needs a centre, direction and angle, not only the instruction 'turn the shape'.
England.classroom_use_en: Require a full description such as 'rotate 90° clockwise about this point'.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grades 1-6 do not contain a systematic rotation-transformation strand; formal geometric transformation standards are mainly in Grade 8.
US.why_en: The primary comparison should show the curriculum-structure difference rather than force a match.
US.classroom_use_en: Use rotations as an extension activity if useful, but do not label them as a formal Common Core Grades 1-6 requirement.
